title: Make wsutil headers include what they use and build standalone
description:
There's many wsutil headers which used glib types like guint8 or GString
but didn't include glib.h. If a new .c file included eg. wsutil/xx.h, it would
not compile if it didn't include glib.h first.
This was also not noticed before because xx.c happened to include glib.h before xx.h.

This commit adds `#include <glib.h>` to the headers in wsutil where it was
missing. It also makes every wsutil/xx.c file include the corresponding
xx.h before including anything else, which makes the build fail if the
header doesn't build standalone due to missing other includes.

---

If people agree this is worth doing, I plan to tackle epan/ as well. I started with wsutil because it's small and doesn't depend on others.

I didn't touch console_win32.c or cfutils.c because I only tested my changes on Linux. I *could* do it blindly and rely on GitLab CI to tell me if I broke something, but it would be better if someone on Windows/Mac makes the change...

This change highlights many headers that are including glib.h only for things like gint, guint32, etc. Is there an ongoing plan to switch them to int, uint32_t, etc? That would remove their dependency on glib.h and I suspect it would make a non-negligible effect in build time (stdint.h is *way* smaller than glib.h!).

notes.body: Why are you still including glib.h if report_message.h already brings it in?

People are [starting to remove glib types](#19116) from several places. That may lead to removing glib.h from foo.h because function signatures don't use gint anymore, but the implementation in foo.c would still need glib.h because it still uses glib functions.

However, maybe I can remove it from the .c, and if someone removes it from the .h it will fail to compile and they will *know* they have to add it back to the .c; it won't go unnoticed. Thoughts?

changed this line in [version 5 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/10861/diffs?diff_id=717251197&start_sha=0c8fc3efcd8f71b79d3b1230fa99643b0e33a545#8957c48672d33d165f2816ac19b94854eec2e1be_22_22)

Moving the header include to the top of the source file in the order was used is a nice cleanup.
```
#include "config.h"
#define WS_LOG_DOMAIN "foo"
#include "source_file.h"
```

Best practice would be to include <wireshark.h> instead of <glib.h>. Please do that if you are going to work on this. This should be done at the top of the header file (source_file.h in the example).

Normally I would be reluctant to use a global header like wireshark.h, since in many projects they tend to be "include everything" monsters, but when I looked at its contents... that actually looks pretty reasonable! It's just system headers, glib.h, and some relatively small Wireshark headers.

Should I replace glib.h with wireshark.h in all these, and move it to the "beginning"? (I think it still makes sense to include config.h before anything)

`wireshark.h` is intentionally kept small and the rules and policies stating that must be strictly adhered to. Yes it should replace `glib.h`. In most cases it will go into the header file only (config.h must always go in the C file). When there is only a C file then yes it should come after config.h (like you said).

As with my comment for report_message.c, I'm not sure about including <glib.h> after you include "report_message.h".  If we do manage to make our individual modules move away from glib types, someone would still need to go back and remove this 2nd inclusion of glib.h.  You might consider the use of glib within the module to be distinct from the API file it includes?

Also, I have long followed (though have not thought about it enough to defend it) the convention of including header files in a C/C++ module in 3 sections, so including (1) after (2) looks odd to me.

(1) system headers that probably won't change until I get a new machine (e.g. glib.h)

(2) library/framework API headers (like in wsutil/epan, etc)

(3) application-level headers (e.g. packet-tcp.h)

I do support adding system-type header files to header files that need them - what do others think?
Is there anything I should change here?
It's just a guide.

This can be removed (because it is already included via `wireshark.h`).

Hmmm I'm not sure about removing these...

Ignoring the glib.h vs wireshark.h for a moment. If foo.c includes foo.h, and foo.h includes glib.h, what if foo.h later *stops* including glib.h because eg. it had the guint32 -> uint32_t conversion done? If foo.c directly uses glib for other reasons (eg. g_malloc or GList), doesn't it make sense that foo.c itself includes glib.h?

See also: https://google.github.io/styleguide/cppguide.html#Include_What_You_Use

I wouldn't mind replacing glib.h with wireshark.h here, or a global rule "every time you would need glib.h, use wireshark.h instead". But I don't think it's a good idea to remove the glib.h/wireshark.h include entirely, since GLib *is* used in ws_mempbrk.c.

But I don't feel too strongly about it, and Martin Mathieson suggested the same earlier :thinking:

(I did remove `ws_symbol_export`, that's not used in the .c file)

Every file must include `wireshark.h`. That's it. In the header file if it exists, in the source file otherwise. `glib.h` and `ws_symbol_export.h` are included via that. It's as simple as that.

IWYU is not a bible. This is not a huge C++ slow monster header. It's a few macros and utility functions that are a requirement for every file and are split over many files and annoying to manage individually.
No one seems to question why we are using a single header for GLib either.
